method.note: Zenodo's free-text search is an OR over the query terms, so the hit counts are large; the candidates were picked by hand from the first page of each query and are listed here with their DOIs so a reader can check each one.

candidates.title: Cell-free DNA fragment files (hg38) from renal cell carcinoma patients and healthy controls
candidates.description: This dataset contains cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragment files generated from plasma of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) patients and healthy control individuals. The dataset comprises 12 samples: - 6 ccRCC patients (labelled PID019, PID020, PID038, PID039, PID040, PID041) - 6 healthy controls (labelled HC001, HC007, HC009, HC010, HC012, HC013) Within the archive, each sample includes two files: - <sample>.hg38.frag.bed.gz: bgzip-compressed BED file of cfDNA fragment coordinates aligned to the human reference genome GRCh38/hg38. - <sample>.hg38.frag.bed.gz.tbi: the corresponding tabix index. A sample metadata table is also provided as zenodo_cfdna_sample_metadata.tsv. Sample identifiers have been coded/de-identified; the file names contain no personal identifiers, and no directly identifying patient information is included in this deposit.

candidates.title: cirDNA End-Motif Frequencies (2- and 4-mers) from sWGS
candidates.description: Processed end-motif frequency tables (2- and 4-mers) from cfDNA shallow WGS. Rows are motifs (ACGT lexicographic), columns are samples; values are per-sample fractions (and counts where provided). Methods: fragment 5′ boundary from paired-end alignments (min reference_start/max reference_end), motifs from reference genome at boundary; primary alignments, proper pairs; duplicates and vendor QC-fail excluded; MAPQ ≥ 30; GRCh38.

candidates.title: LEAF-1 pretraining corpus: cfDNA fragments
candidates.description: This record documents the cell-free DNA (cfDNA) portion of the pretraining corpus of LEAF-1, a DNA language model of cell-free DNA and chromatin-accessibility fragments. The fragment files themselves (211 GB bgzip-compressed, 34.0 billion fragments) are too large for Zenodo and are hosted on Hugging Face: huggingface.co/datasets/jing-z/leaf1-pretraining-cfdna . Paper: bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.09.737627 scATAC-seq portion of the pretraining corpus: 10.5281/zenodo.23176597 TCGA ATAC-seq portion (controlled access; sample manifest and processing code): 10.5281/zenodo.23195360 This record contains the sample manifest and md5 checksums of the uncompressed and compressed files. Fragments derive from FinaleDB (Zheng et al., 2021, Bioinformatics) and the studies of Adalsteinsson et al. 2017, Cristiano et al. 2019, Jiang et al. 2015 and Sun et al. 2019; please cite them when reusing the data.

candidates.title: SAUNA paper - cfDNA Fragment dataset
candidates.description: SAUNA - Simulated Annealing for Unique Nucleosome Arrangements The dataset contains the data used in the publication of the SAUNA tool. 9 medium coverage (14-30x) cfDNA-sequencing files were mapped to the hg38 build of the human genome using bwa mem. Mapped sequence (Bam) files were converted into paired-end bed files using the `bedtools -pe` command. Consequently, the fragment information was extracted using the following commands. gunzip -c $file | awk 'BEGIN {OFS="\t"} $1 == $4 && ($6 - $2) <= 2000' | cut --output-delimiter=$'\t' -f1,2,6,8,9 | sort -k1,1V -k2,2n -k3,3n | bgzip > "${file%.sortByName.bed.gz}_hg38.frag.tsv.bgz" The resulting data files do not contain sequence information but can be converted back into bam files using Fragmentstein (https://github.com/uzh-dqbm-cmi/fragmentstein/, https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article/40/1/btae017/7550024) and can be used for most analyses relevant in cfDNA-sequencing, with the exception of calling point mutations.
